appraisal_events.evidence: Bloch's family and coreligionists form "un cortège homogène en soi" that the Cambremer set, the premier président's clan and the bourgeois "retrouvaient là tous les ans sans jamais échanger un salut avec eux"; Bloch feels the hostility and fronts it "en une phalange compacte et close où personne d'ailleurs ne songeait à se frayer un chemin".
appraisal_events.explanation: The Balbec resort world is shown withholding even a greeting year after year, so Bloch's set is held wholly outside a social space no one on either side crosses.

appraisal_events.evidence: "les Stones of Venaïce, de Lord John Ruskin" leads the narrator to conclude that Bloch believes every English male is a lord and that i is always pronounced aï; caught out on "lift", he answers "d'un ton sec et hautain": "Cela n'a d'ailleurs aucune espèce d'importance", a phrase the narrator reads as proof of how much it does matter to him.
appraisal_events.explanation: Bloch's display of cosmopolitan erudition collapses into exposed ignorance, and his attempt to recover the upper hand in talk is dissected as wounded self-love.

appraisal_events.evidence: Fearing Bloch might later think himself laughed at, Robert "se sentit coupable comme s'il avait manqué de l'indulgence dont il débordait", and the blush that would one day rise to Bloch's face "il la sentit par anticipation et réversibilité monter au sien".
appraisal_events.explanation: In the same exchange that exposes Bloch, Saint-Loup is credited with a delicacy so fine that he feels another man's future shame in advance.

appraisal_events.evidence: After the tactless "es-tu snob ?" put to the narrator, the long meditation on the defect one cannot see in oneself ("le snob des snobs") closes flatly: "Bloch était mal élevé, névropathe, snob, et, appartenant à une famille peu estimée, supportait comme au fond des mers les incalculables pressions" of the Christian world and of the superior Jewish castes above his own.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator states an unhedged verdict on Bloch's character and, with it, on the low esteem of his family and the depth from which he would have to climb.

status_effects.explanation: The passage shows a hard, mutually observed line at Balbec: his set is looked at, never greeted, and remains a closed phalanx no one enters or leaves.
He loses the exchange twice over — first by the blunder, then by the haughty disclaimer that betrays how much the correction stung.
The narration's summary judgment is severe and unqualified: ill-bred, neurotic, snobbish, and blind to the fault he detects in others.
Distinct from the beach-society boundary, his standing is reported as low within his own world too: a family 'peu estimée', pressed on by every caste above it.
His anticipatory blush on Bloch's behalf is presented as genuine fineness of feeling, raising him in the same scene that lowers his friend.

ambiguities: The description of Bloch's milieu is voiced largely through the hostile onlookers ('cette horde de fillasses mal élevées' falls inside what the grainetiers' daughters would refuse), and the narrator then relativizes it — 'ce milieu devait renfermer comme tout autre, peut-être plus que tout autre, beaucoup d'agréments' — so how far the contempt is the narration's own remains unsettled, even though the exclusion itself is reported as fact.
